Exact Rank Profiles from Euclidean Coordinates

Source: R/coordinate-ranks.R
exact_rank_profiles.Rd

Compare several embeddings against the same candidate neighbors. For each query, compute its reference ranks once, score every embedding, then release the ranks before moving to the next query.

Usage

exact_rank_profiles(Xin, embeddings, k, mrre = FALSE, query_rows = NULL)

Arguments

Xin

Dense reference coordinates with observations in rows.

embeddings

A nonempty list of dense coordinate matrices or data frames with the same observations in the same order as Xin. Pass list(y) for a single embedding. Nonnumeric data-frame columns are ignored. All coordinate values must be finite.

k

Unique neighborhood sizes, each positive and less than half the number of observations. This range supports both rank penalties.

mrre

Logical. Include mean relative rank errors (MRRE) for input neighbors and output neighbors? Defaults to FALSE.

query_rows

Optional vector of unique, one-based row positions in Xin to score, in the requested order. The default (NULL) scores all rows. Each query still ranks all other observations, including rows outside the selection.

Value

A list in embedding order, retaining the names of embeddings. Each entry contains pointwise trustworthiness and continuity matrices, the RNX auc vector, and the RNX curve matrix at the requested sizes. The integer matrix retained counts neighbors shared by the reference and embedding among the first k other observations. Divide a column by its k to get the unadjusted fraction retained. Rows retain the selected reference row names. Column means summarize the selected queries. With mrre = TRUE, each entry also contains mrre_input and mrre_output matrices at the requested sizes. Smaller errors indicate better rank preservation.

Details

Each row's candidate pool contains all other observations. Tied Euclidean distances follow observation order, as with pointwise_rank_preservation() and pointwise_rnx() on matrices from stats::dist(). RNX AUC uses every size from one through n - 2.

For MRRE, select the first k neighbors in one space. For each of these neighbors, divide the absolute change in rank by its rank in the selecting space. Sum and divide by sum((n - 2 * r) / r) over ranks 1 through k. Identical rankings give zero and reversed rankings give one. For large neighborhoods, other permutations can exceed one under this normalization.

Scaling

Keep all N rows of the coordinates. Each of q selected queries computes and sorts N - 1 distances per space. Scoring all rows requires quadratic distance work, and wide inputs make each distance more expensive. Temporary rank workspace grows linearly with N. Output size grows with the number of queries, requested neighborhood sizes, and embeddings.

For a large-data audit, sample query_rows and reuse them for every embedding. Each score is exact for its query against the full pool. The column means summarize the sampled queries. Slicing Xin and the embeddings before the call changes the candidate pool and can change the scores.

References

Venna and Kaski (2001) give the rank penalties for trustworthiness and continuity. doi:10.1007/3-540-44668-0_68

Lee et al. (2013) define RNX. Lee, Peluffo-Ordóñez and Verleysen (2015) summarize the curve with weights proportional to 1 / k. doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2012.12.036 and doi:10.1016/j.neucom.2014.12.095

Lee and Verleysen (2008) give the two mean relative rank errors in equations 5 and 6. Quadra reports the errors directly, with zero for agreement. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v4/lee08a.html ZADU 0.5.4 instead reports one minus the normalized error.

Examples

x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
y <- prcomp(x)$x[, 1:2]
profile <- exact_rank_profiles(x, list(PCA = y), k = c(5, 15), mrre = TRUE)
colMeans(profile$PCA$mrre_input)
#>         k5        k15 
#> 0.01600334 0.02117424 
set.seed(42)
queries <- sample.int(nrow(x), 30)
spot <- exact_rank_profiles(x, list(PCA = y), k = 5, query_rows = queries)
colMeans(spot$PCA$curve) # 30 queries, 149 candidates per query
#>      rnx5 
#> 0.6412963
